title: Bubble, selection and insertion sort
summary: Three O(n²) sorts, watched pass by pass, and the one that is genuinely useful.

steps.title: Bubble sort
body: **Bubble sort** walks the array comparing neighbours and swaps any pair that is out of order. After the first pass the biggest value has "bubbled" to the end; after the second, the second biggest; and so on.
That is why the inner loop stops at `a.Length - 1 - i`: the last `i` slots are already final.
Step through and watch the boxes swap. Two nested loops: `O(n²)` comparisons.

code: for (var j = 0; j < a.Length - 1 - i; j++)

steps.prompt: This bubble sort stops after its **second** pass. What does the array look like?
code: for (var j = 0; j < a.Length - 1 - i; j++)
steps.explain: Pass 1 carries the 5 to the end: `2,4,1,3,5`. Pass 2 carries the 4 to its place: `2,1,3,4,5`. Only one swap is left to do.
hints: Do pass 1 on paper: compare 5 and 2, swap; 5 and 4, swap; and so on.

steps.title: Selection sort
body: **Selection sort** thinks the other way round: find the **smallest** remaining value and swap it into the next position.
Every pass scans the whole unsorted part (`O(n²)` comparisons) but makes at most **one** swap. Watch `min` track the smallest value seen in each scan.

code: for (var j = i + 1; j < a.Length; j++)

steps.prompt: Selection sort on `4 3 1 2`. Arrange the array states from the start (top) to sorted (bottom), one state per pass.
steps.explain: Pass 1 swaps the 1 to the front, pass 2 swaps the 2 into slot 1, pass 3 swaps the 3 into slot 2.

steps.title: Insertion sort
body: **Insertion sort** is how you sort a hand of cards. Keep the left part sorted; take the next item and slide it left past every bigger item until it fits.
On **nearly sorted** data each item only slides a step or two, so it runs close to `O(n)`. That is why real libraries use it for small or almost-sorted pieces.
Watch `key` being held while bigger values shift right one box.

steps.prompt: Insertion sort, stopped after it has inserted `a[2]`. What does it print?
steps.explain: Inserting 2 gives `2,5,4,6,1`; inserting 4 slides it past the 5: `2,4,5,6,1`. The right part is untouched so far.

steps.prompt: Match each sort to its signature move.
pairs: swaps neighbours; the largest drifts to the end
finds the minimum, one swap per pass
slides each item left into a sorted prefix
O(n²) comparisons in the worst case

steps.prompt: Complete the insertion sort's inner loop.
steps.explain: Shift bigger values one slot right. When the loop stops, `j` sits just left of the gap, so the key goes into `j + 1`.

steps.title: Write two sorts
prompt: Write two in-place sorts for `int[]`, ascending:
No `Array.Sort`, `OrderBy` or `List.Sort`. Tuple swaps `(a[i], a[j]) = (a[j], a[i])` are fine.
solution: for (var j = i + 1; j < a.Length; j++)
template: Dojo.Eq("InsertionSort is fast on nearly sorted data", 10, dojoNearly[10]);

forbid.message: Does not call a library sort

hints: Selection: for each `i`, find the index of the smallest value from `i` onwards, then swap it into `i`.
Insertion: copy the trace from the card. Hold `key = a[i]`, shift bigger values right, drop `key` into `j + 1`.
